# id: # trigger: short | correction | long | error | any. adopt_regex: an ERE matched against a later prompt in
# the same session; "-" means adoption is not detectable. Keep each text under 100 characters.

text: Say what done looks like: the file, the check to run, the expected result.
Corrected twice? /clear and restart with one sharper prompt that holds what you learned.
Long session: /compact <what matters next> keeps answers sharp and cheaper.
Paste the exact error and command; a paraphrase makes the agent guess.
Ask for proof: "run the tests and show the output" beats "is it done?".
Point at code with @path/to/file instead of describing where it lives.
For multi-file changes, ask for a plan first (Shift+Tab to plan mode), then approve.
One goal per prompt; queue the next one after this one is verified.
Going the wrong way? Press Esc to stop it mid-turn, then redirect in one line.
Press Esc twice (or /rewind) to roll code and chat back to an earlier point.
Pick an old chat back up with /resume, or start with claude --continue.
Run /context to see what fills the context window before it runs out.
Repeating an instruction? Put it in CLAUDE.md once; /memory opens it.
New repo? /init writes a starter CLAUDE.md from the codebase.
Start a line with ! to run a shell command yourself; the output lands in the chat.
Show, don't describe: paste a screenshot of the UI or error with Ctrl+V.
Big search? Ask for a subagent so the file dumps stay out of your context.
Same prompt again? Save it as .claude/commands/<name>.md and run /<name>.
Approving the same safe command again? Allow it once in /permissions.
Use /model: a faster model for small edits, a stronger one for hard bugs.
Type your next message while Claude works; it reads it at the next step.
For scripts and cron: claude -p "<prompt>" prints the answer and exits.
Work spans two repos? /add-dir lets Claude read and edit the second folder.
Want it every time (format, lint)? Make it a hook in /hooks, not a reminder.
Show one example of the output you want; it beats a paragraph of description.
For a bug, ask for a failing test first, then the fix that makes it pass.
Before you commit, ask Claude to review its own diff for bugs.
